uniequip_002_thumpy:
'Aiyaya... I'll never finish all this. I'm only going to be gone five or six days, there's really no need for such a grand send-off...' That was her own flustered voice.
'What was that, Thumpy dear—the carrot roast isn't enough—' That was her father's voice, all but drowned out by the racket of the kitchen.
'Er...' Tani remembers why her own voice cut off right there. Her father's carrot roast was her favorite dish in the world—but it had occurred to her at once that she would not be there for the next day's bone stew with wild greens. Setting off on a long journey was always exciting, yet the business of 'leaving home' left her a little wistful all the same.
'Everything's on the table, let the send-off feast begin—' That was her mother's cheerful voice, followed by the thumping footsteps of the whole extended family drawing nearer, and in an instant Tani was buried under a chattering, effusive avalanche of well-wishes. Never mind that her ears had been ringing at the time; even now she cannot make out what any of them were actually saying. She can guess, though. Stay safe on the road, bring back some local specialties, write to us—that sort of thing.
She must have noticed, back then, that her father looked rather ill at ease.
'Thumpy dear, um...' Her father hemmed and hawed, quite unlike himself. 'Tell us what present you really want. Your mother and I, and your uncles and your aunts and all your cousins on both sides... we're all ready to listen properly to your voice.'
...
So the house had gone quiet for that long. And then she hears a snort—that was her, laughing.
'Dad, you're so awkward when you apologize. And you dragged all these people along just to work up the nerve.'
'Ahem, ahem...'
'But I don't want a new present. Even if I'm not a switchboard operator anymore, I still want to treasure the feelings everyone put into my birthday gifts.'
'But...'
'Mom, weren't we agreed that you'd listen to my voice this time? Actually, I only need everyone to do me one favor~ Mm, I know I'm setting off soon, but if the whole family pitches in, I'm sure we can get it done before I go!'
In a wind-scoured hollow where hardly a soul ever treads, Tani lies contentedly in her massage rocking chair. She takes a bite of a carrot crisp, coated with a layer of caramel boiled down from throat lozenges. Mm—the lozenges really do give it a strange flavor, and the caramel is a touch too burnt, but that suits her clumsy, endearing cousins perfectly. Beneath her sits the seriously cool—massage-rocking-chair-mobile, fitted with an Originium combustion engine and off-road tires. She drove this beast all the way out here, and once she reached her destination and pried the shell off, it became a picnic chair with a massage function. The glued-together shell is not exactly sturdy, and the seat rocked so relentlessly while she drove that she nearly threw up on the control panel—but building it together with everyone was genuinely, enormously fun.
And then... the headphones her parents gave her, and the switchboard they refitted especially so it would work with a music player. She picked it up meaning to listen to some music, and found this rowdy recording that had survived by accident.
